definitions.explanation: A feeling of sorrow and concern for the suffering or misfortune of others. Can carry a slightly condescending nuance depending on context.

examples.japanese: {憐|あわ}れみの{目|め}で{見|み}られた。
examples.english: I was looked at with eyes of pity.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}にも{憐|あわ}れみを{持|も}つべきだ。
examples.english: One should have mercy even toward enemies.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いて、{憐|あわ}れみの{気持|きも}ちが{込|こ}み{上|あ}げてきた。
examples.english: Listening to her story, a feeling of compassion welled up inside me.

notes:
USAGE:
Also written as {哀|あわ}れみ, though {憐|あわ}れみ is more common when emphasizing compassion toward someone's suffering. When used with の{目|め}で{見|み}る (to look at with eyes of pity), it often implies a condescending feeling that the recipient may not welcome.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {憐|あわ}れみを{感|かん}じる (to feel pity)
- {憐|あわ}れみの{目|め} (eyes of pity)
- {憐|あわ}れみを{乞|こ}う (to beg for mercy)
- {憐|あわ}れみを{持|も}つ (to have compassion)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {同情|どうじょう}: sympathy — more neutral, less condescending
- {慈悲|じひ}: mercy, benevolence — Buddhist/religious tone, more elevated
- {思|おも}いやり: consideration, thoughtfulness — warmer, without the pity nuance
